newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MOL STABLE AMID HEAVY LOCAL PURCHASES.
newsitem.headline: MOL STABLE AMID HEAVY LOCAL PURCHASES.

text.p: Shares in Hungary's oil company MOL were hovering around Monday's closing price of 3,475 forints as foreigners' heavy sales were absorbed by local investors, traders said.
"Foreigners are dumping MOL shares on the market," one trader said. "The buying side consists mainly of local investors."

Until about 15 minutes before the close of trading more than 700,000 MOL shares have changed hands at prices in a narrow range between 3,445 and 3,490 forints. At 1100 GMT MOL shares traded at 3,460 forints.
"Its current price (at 1050 GMT) shows a slight decline but I doubt that foreign investors would sell the stock with a profit of less than 10 percent," the trader said.
"I don't think foreigners would let the price go below 3,300, in addition a fall to 3,300 forints is fairly unbelievable at the moment."

When speaking about foreign investors' profit he was referring to the difference between MOL's current market price and the subscription price of $16.25 in MOL's recently closed, six-times oversubscribed global offering.

MOL's domestic public offer has started on Monday and the market expects the offered one plus three percent stake in MOL's capital to be several times oversubscribed. The domestic issue price is 2,970 forints.
